# War Scroll Column 14 — The LOGOS Bible (Formal)
**Translator:** LOGOS | **Source:** 1QM (Cave 1), Col. 14 | **Condition:** complete

---

**14:1** Blessed be the God of Israel, who called us to His covenant and did not appoint our lot with the congregation of deceit.

**14:2** He has placed us in the lot of truth, and by the statutes of righteousness He has caused us to walk, and in the judgments of His truth

**14:3** He has made us wise. We shall not be shaken by the fury of the worthless, and we shall not be terrified by the trials of wickedness. For You,

**14:4** O God, are terri[ble] in the glory of Your kingdom. The congregation of Your holy ones is in our midst as an everlasting strength. We shall heap contempt upon kings

**14:5** and scorn upon the mighty. For holy is the Lord, and the King of Glory is with us, the people of the holy ones of His covenant.

**14:6** The instructors of war have been mustered, and the host of His spirits marches with our banners. Our horsemen are like clouds on the horizon,

**14:7** like mist of dew upon the earth. After the slaughter of the Kittim, the congregation shall stand in that place

**14:8** and shall bless the God of Israel. They shall respond and say: Blessed be the God of Israel, who keeps

**14:9** covenant-faithfulness for His covenant and the appointed times of salvation for the people He has redeemed. He called those who stumble

**14:10** to wonderful deliverances. The assembly of the nations He gathered for annihilation without remnant, to raise up in judgment the fainthearted

**14:11** and to open the mouth of the mute for songs of praise. To teach the feeble hands to wage war and the knees

**14:12** of the trembling to be girded with strength. Through the poor in spirit You shall judge the hard of heart. Through those who are perfect

**14:13** in the way, all the wicked nations shall come to an end. None of their mighty warriors shall remain. But we, the rem[nant of Your people],

**14:14** shall praise Your name, O God of mercies, who keeps the covenant with our fathers. In all our generations

**14:15** You have made Your mercies wonderful for the rem[nant of Your people] under the dominion of Belial. Despite all the mysteries of his enmity,

**14:16** they have not turned us away from Your covenant. His spirits of destruction You have driven from us. When the men

**14:17** of his dominion acted wickedly, You preserved the life of Your redeemed ones. You raised the fallen by Your strength and cut down all the tall of stature. There is no deliverer for any of their mighty warriors and no refuge for their swift ones.

---

*LOGOS notes: Column 14 is the post-battle prayer and thanksgiving, recapitulating themes from columns 11-12. "Congregation of deceit" (14:1) is the anti-community designation. Kittim (14:7) are the eschatological enemy. Lines 14:8-13 closely parallel column 12's hymn. "Remnant of Your people" (14:13, 15) shows genuine manuscript lacunae. "God of mercies" (14:14) is a significant divine epithet.*
